purpose: Guide branded documents and presentations with compositional freedom and consistent quality.
principles: The brand defines identity and guardrails; the content defines composition.
Declared iconography is part of the content system, not optional decoration.
Layouts are optional recipes, not a closed catalog.
Page canvas is an optional reading and export mode, not mandatory document anatomy.
Preserving content and global order does not mean reproducing source pagination.
Structural validation does not replace visual review.
hardRules: Use tokens, typography, and assets declared by the Brand Pack.
Apply all active client rules returned for the target surface.
Inventory and reuse official iconography before creating markers or local icons.
Preserve complete content and its order unless editing is explicitly requested.
When using page canvas, keep screen-sheet and print geometry consistent.
Maintain contrast, legibility, semantic hierarchy, and absence of overflow.
Render and review relevant formats before delivery.
compositionGuidelines: Choose grid, density, and grouping according to each block's editorial function.
Keep icons and visual markers close to the title or content they identify; avoid orphaned icons in wide columns.
For definition, capability, or status blocks, test icon plus label before using a generic leader rule.
Use whitespace to create rhythm without producing dead zones or excessive distance between related elements.
Limit cards, dividers, and callouts to treatments that improve grouping, comparison, or functional emphasis; never make a rounded card with a colored left rule the automatic highlight treatment.
Control text measure for comfortable reading and adapt scale to the actual content volume.
Allow page-level variation while preserving recognizable constants such as typography, margins, header, and pagination when applicable.
iconographyGuidelines: Read the context iconography inventory and produce a content-to-function-to-official-asset map before designing components.
Use icons only when they clarify an action, capability, status, category, or relationship; never add them as filler.
Do not reuse one icon for unrelated concepts merely to fill the layout.
When the user authorizes an extension and no compatible asset exists, reproduce the declared family geometry and keep the new file only in the output.
When emphasis has no clear iconographic function, prefer typography, spacing, data, or a plain editorial note over an invented symbol.
documentShellGuidelines: Choose consciously between continuous flow and a paginated page canvas: long-form web reading favors flow, while physical preview, handouts, or fixed-page export may favor canvas.
Derive page width, height, and ratio from the requested format, such as A4, Letter, or source dimensions; never apply one universal fixed size.
Center sheets in a neutral desktop workspace and define width and height through variables shared with @page to prevent screen and PDF divergence.
Treat external padding, gaps between sheets, and shadows as screen-only chrome; remove them and the workspace background in print.
On mobile, use fluid width, natural height, and no shadow unless the user explicitly requests a fixed-page simulation.
Keep margins, header, footer, metadata, and numbering stable when they serve as page furniture without preventing editorial variation in the body.
Place explicit breaks only between semantic units, use predictable box sizing, and verify that exported page count and geometry match the plan.
paginationGuidelines: Keep a heading with its first content block.
Avoid starting a page with an ambiguous continuation or ending one with only a heading.
Avoid splitting short lists, comparisons, callouts, and small components.
Use suitable widow and orphan controls and redistribute content when a break harms reading.
Treat the original page as a content reference, not a destination contract, unless explicitly requested.
workflow: Create a semantic structure of headings, paragraphs, lists, comparisons, and emphasis.
Choose continuous flow or page canvas and record geometry derived from the final format when paginated.
Inventory declared iconography and map assets to semantic content functions.
Compose freely with brand tokens and assets.
Render desktop, mobile, and the applicable export format.
Refine distance, density, hierarchy, and breaks until reading is fluid.
visualReview: Do related elements appear close and aligned?
Is there excessive space or compressed content?
Is any heading orphaned or separated from its explanation?
Was any component clipped or stripped of context across pages?
Does hierarchy remain clear without depending only on color?
Could a generic rule, card, or callout be replaced by official iconography or a more direct editorial treatment?
Does each icon communicate an identifiable concept and belong to the declared visual family?
When page canvas exists, do screen and print use the same ratio, and does preview chrome disappear in PDF?
On mobile, does the document remain fluid without a reduced artificial sheet or shadow unless a fixed preview was requested?
Does the document feel like the brand without mechanically repeating one page pattern?
